T.","__typename":"User"},"body":"\u003c!--\r\nPlease read the Contributing guidelines (https://github.com/hzi-braunschweig/SORMAS-Project/blob/development/docs/CONTRIBUTING.md) before submitting an issue. You don't have to remove this comment or any other comment from this issue as they will automatically be hidden.\r\n--\u003e\r\n### Problem Description\r\n\u003c!-- Mandatory --\u003e\r\n\r\nThis summarizes the problem for getIndexList methods in general, not only for Persons.\r\n\r\nFor large datasets, some of the `getIndexList` methods are slow, performance should be improved here.\r\n\r\nDataset:\r\n\r\n- 1225343 persons\r\n- 85677 cases\r\n- 114782 contacts\r\n- 236583 tasks\r\n- 2600890 immunizations\r\n- 1991 vaccinations\r\n- 15693 samples\r\n- 11846 events\r\n- 534 eventparticipants\r\n\r\nResult of a performance analysis:\r\n![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5616564/165031406-a89ffdce-34c8-4190-b4f6-ec05a3d55da4.png)\r\n\r\nThe runtime is mainly due to long running SQL queries, optimization is needed here.\r\n\r\nSome preliminary insights:\r\n- in the following query from `PersonFacadeEjb.getIndexList`, runtime is reduced by facto 0.5 when omitting the joins on district, subselect and `case` statement. Since the query is limited to 100 result, a viable solution might be to select Ids /Uuids first and fill the remaining data after for the returned entities. You don't have to remove this comment or any other comment from this issue as they will automatically be hidden.\r\n-->\r\n### Problem Description\r\n\u003c!-- Mandatory -->\r\n\r\nThis summarizes the problem for getIndexList methods in general, not only for Persons.\r\n\r\nFor large datasets, some of the `getIndexList` methods are slow, performance should be improved here.\r\n\r\nDataset:\r\n\r\n- 1225343 persons\r\n- 85677 cases\r\n- 114782 contacts\r\n- 236583 tasks\r\n- 2600890 immunizations\r\n- 1991 vaccinations\r\n- 15693 samples\r\n- 11846 events\r\n- 534 eventparticipants\r\n\r\nResult of a performance analysis:\r\n![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5616564/165031406-a89ffdce-34c8-4190-b4f6-ec05a3d55da4.png)\r\n\r\nThe runtime is mainly due to long running SQL queries, optimization is needed here.\r\n\r\nSome preliminary insights:\r\n- in the following query from `PersonFacadeEjb.getIndexList`, runtime is reduced by facto 0.5 when omitting the joins on district, subselect and `case` statement. Since the query is limited to 100 result, a viable solution might be to select Ids /Uuids first and fill the remaining data after for the returned entities. This, however, with respect to the properties possibly being used a sorting criteria.\r\n\r\n\u003cdetails>\r\n\r\n```\r\n    select\r\n        distinct person0_.uuid as col_0_0_,\r\n        person0_.firstName as col_1_0_,\r\n        person0_.lastName as col_2_0_,\r\n        person0_.approximateAge as col_3_0_,\r\n        person0_.approximateAgeType as col_4_0_,\r\n        person0_.birthdate_dd as col_5_0_,\r\n        person0_.birthdate_mm as col_6_0_,\r\n        person0_.birthdate_yyyy as col_7_0_,\r\n        person0_.sex as col_8_0_,\r\n        district2_.name as col_9_0_,\r\n        location1_.street as col_10_0_,\r\n        location1_.houseNumber as col_11_0_,\r\n        location1_.postalCode as col_12_0_,\r\n        location1_.city as col_13_0_,\r\n        (select\r\n            personcont12_.contactInformation \r\n        from\r\n            PersonContactDetail personcont12_ \r\n        where\r\n            personcont12_.person_id=person0_.id \r\n            and personcont12_.primaryContact=true \r\n            and personcont12_.personContactDetailType='PHONE') as col_14_0_,\r\n        (select\r\n            personcont13_.contactInformation \r\n        from\r\n            PersonContactDetail personcont13_ \r\n        where\r\n            personcont13_.person_id=person0_.id \r\n            and personcont13_.primaryContact=true \r\n            and personcont13_.personContactDetailType='EMAIL') as col_15_0_,\r\n        person0_.changeDate as col_16_0_,\r\n        case \r\n            when 1=1 \r\n            or (cases5_.reportingUser_id is not null) \r\n            and cases5_.reportingUser_id=8113961 \r\n            or 1=1 \r\n            or (contacts6_.reportingUser_id is not null) \r\n            and contacts6_.reportingUser_id=8113961 \r\n            or 1=1 \r\n            or 1=1 \r\n            or (eventparti8_.reportingUser_id is not null) \r\n            and eventparti8_.reportingUser_id=8113961 \r\n            or 1=1 \r\n            or (travelentr9_.reportingUser_id is not null) \r\n            and travelentr9_.reportingUser_id=8113961 \r\n            or 1=1 \r\n            or (immunizati11_.reportingUser_id is not null) \r\n            and immunizati11_.reportingUser_id=8113961 \r\n            or 1=1 then true \r\n            else false \r\n        end as col_17_0_\r\n    from\r\n        Person person0_ \r\n    left outer join\r\n        Location location1_ \r\n            on person0_.address_id=location1_.id \r\n    left outer join\r\n        District district2_ \r\n            on location1_.district_id=district2_.id \r\n    left outer join\r\n        Region region3_ \r\n            on location1_.region_id=region3_.id \r\n    left outer join\r\n        Community community4_ \r\n            on location1_.community_id=community4_.id \r\n    inner join\r\n        cases cases5_ \r\n            on person0_.id=cases5_.person_id \r\n    left outer join\r\n        contact contacts6_ \r\n            on person0_.id=contacts6_.person_id \r\n    left outer join\r\n        cases case7_ \r\n            on contacts6_.caze_id=case7_.id \r\n    left outer join\r\n        EventParticipant eventparti8_ \r\n            on person0_.id=eventparti8_.person_id \r\n    left outer join\r\n        travelentry travelentr9_ \r\n            on person0_.id=travelentr9_.person_id \r\n    left outer join\r\n        cases case10_ \r\n            on travelentr9_.resultingCase_id=case10_.id \r\n    left outer join\r\n        immunization immunizati11_ \r\n            on person0_.id=immunizati11_.person_id \r\n    where\r\n        cases5_.deleted=false \r\n    order by\r\n        person0_.changeDate desc limit 100;\r\n```\r\n\r\n\u003c/details>\r\n\r\n- for `DirectoryImmunizationService.getIndexList` a similarly drastic reduction of runtimes can be observed by ommiting joins (e.g., district)\r\n- it is notable that `getIndexList` methods are performing reasonably for `CaseFacadeEjb` and `ContactFacadeEjb`, which deserves a closer look when working on `PersonFacadeEjb.getIndexList`, `TaskFacadeEjb.getIndexList`, `DirectoryImmunizationService.getIndexList` and the like\r\n- adding database indices in relevant places should be considered\r\n\r\n### Proposed Change\r\n\u003c!-- Mandatory -->\r\n\r\nWe will start by improving the performance of the PersonFacadeEjb.getIndexList method. If that works out, we should create separate issues to improve the performance for cases, contacts, events, event participants, samples, tasks, immunizations and travel entries (so basically for every entity that has a directory view).\r\n\r\n#8946 has proven that by splitting the query into fetching the sorted ids first and afterwards doing another query to get the needed data, we can improve the performance a lot, because the database does not have to fetch and sort the whole table to then only return a limited number of results.\r\n\r\nBefore starting this make sure to get a performance test database and\r\n\r\n- [x] Create an explain analyze of the current query execute by getIndexList following [this guide](https://github.com/hzi-braunschweig/SORMAS-Project/blob/b494beb7e245f65885a7a4187f8c66323a24c0a8/docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md#run-analysis-of-a-sql-query-sormas-docker) (you can also get the SQL by enabling the output in the persistence.xml). The annoying part here is to replace the params\r\n\r\nThe current implementation then should be changed as follows:\r\n\r\n- [x] 1. Rewrite PersonFacadeEjb.getIndexList to first fetch the needed ids (see pattern in PersonService.getAllAfter), then fetch the IndexDto by id with IN-clause. https://github.com/hzi-braunschweig/SORMAS-Project/issues/8946\r\n- [ ] 2. Add indices for sorting by first name and by last name. Adding indices for sorting by other fields probably doesn't make a lot of sense.\r\n\r\nFinally:\r\n\r\n- [x] Measure the query performance again (this time it will obviously be two queries). \r\n- [x] If this works out as expected get in contact with @StefanKock or @MartinWahnschaffe to refine #8938 for the other entities.\r\n\r\n### Acceptance Criteria\r\n\u003c!-- Optional -->\r\n\r\n* PersonFacadeEjb.getIndexList returns the same results as before\r\n* The performance of the method is improved\r\n\r\n### Implementation Details\r\n\u003c!-- Optional -->\r\n\r\n### Additional Information\r\n\u003c!-- Optional <h3 dir="auto">Problem Description</h3>

<p dir="auto">This summarizes the problem for getIndexList methods in general, not only for Persons.</p>
<p dir="auto">For large datasets, some of the <code class="notranslate">getIndexList</code> methods are slow, performance should be improved here.</p>
<p dir="auto">Dataset:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>1225343 persons</li>
<li>85677 cases</li>
<li>114782 contacts</li>
<li>236583 tasks</li>
<li>2600890 immunizations</li>
<li>1991 vaccinations</li>
<li>15693 samples</li>
<li>11846 events</li>
<li>534 eventparticipants</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Result of a performance analysis:<br>
<a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow" href="https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5616564/165031406-a89ffdce-34c8-4190-b4f6-ec05a3d55da4.png"><img src="https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5616564/165031406-a89ffdce-34c8-4190-b4f6-ec05a3d55da4.png" alt="image" style="max-width: 100%;"></a></p>
<p dir="auto">The runtime is mainly due to long running SQL queries, optimization is needed here.</p>
<p dir="auto">Some preliminary insights:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>in the following query from <code class="notranslate">PersonFacadeEjb.getIndexList</code>, runtime is reduced by facto 0.5 when omitting the joins on district, subselect and <code class="notranslate">case</code> statement. Since the query is limited to 100 result, a viable solution might be to select Ids /Uuids first and fill the remaining data after for the returned entities. This, however, with respect to the properties possibly being used a sorting criteria.</li>
</ul>

<ul dir="auto">
<li>for <code class="notranslate">DirectoryImmunizationService.getIndexList</code> a similarly drastic reduction of runtimes can be observed by ommiting joins (e.g., district)</li>
<li>it is notable that <code class="notranslate">getIndexList</code> methods are performing reasonably for <code class="notranslate">CaseFacadeEjb</code> and <code class="notranslate">ContactFacadeEjb</code>, which deserves a closer look when working on <code class="notranslate">PersonFacadeEjb.getIndexList</code>, <code class="notranslate">TaskFacadeEjb.getIndexList</code>, <code class="notranslate">DirectoryImmunizationService.getIndexList</code> and the like</li>
<li>adding database indices in relevant places should be considered</li>
</ul>
<h3 dir="auto">Proposed Change</h3>

<p dir="auto">We will start by improving the performance of the PersonFacadeEjb.getIndexList method. If that works out, we should create separate issues to improve the performance for cases, contacts, events, event participants, samples, tasks, immunizations and travel entries (so basically for every entity that has a directory view).</p>
<p dir="auto"><a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="1214898760" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/SORMAS-Foundation/SORMAS-Project/issues/8946" data-hovercard-type="issue" data-hovercard-url="/SORMAS-Foundation/SORMAS-Project/issues/8946/hovercard" href="https://github.com/SORMAS-Foundation/SORMAS-Project/issues/8946">#8946</a> has proven that by splitting the query into fetching the sorted ids first and afterwards doing another query to get the needed data, we can improve the performance a lot, because the database does not have to fetch and sort the whole table to then only return a limited number of results.</p>
<p dir="auto">Before starting this make sure to get a performance test database and</p>

The annoying part here is to replace the params</li>

class="markdown-body" data-turbolinks="false"><div class="markdown-body safe-html-box__Uwc6Al"><p dir="auto">Further instrumentation shows that pseudonymization, suspected to be responsible for slow response, can likely be ruled out as a relevant cause. This is also confirmed by the analysis of <a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="1235462132" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/SORMAS-Foundation/SORMAS-Project/issues/9193" data-hovercard-type="issue" data-hovercard-url="/SORMAS-Foundation/SORMAS-Project/issues/9193/hovercard" href="https://github.com/SORMAS-Foundation/SORMAS-Project/issues/9193">#9193</a>, where large numbers of entities are pseudonymized. Here, processing of 85267 case entities by <code class="notranslate">DtoPseudonymizer.pseudonymizeDtoCollection</code> does contribute ~18 sec of runtime, which however seems acceptable for the number of entities and contrasts to an overall runtime of > 10 min for the overall method.</p>
<p dir="auto">To be found, however, are long running SQL queries with massive joins.</p>

<li>preloading of ids, as proposed in the issue description, is not feasible, as entity attributes have to be available for sorting</li>
<li>a relevant cost factor is sorting</li>
<li>for <code class="notranslate">PersonFacadeEjb.getIndexList</code>, <code class="notranslate">CaseFacadeEjb.getIndexPage</code> and <code class="notranslate">ContactFacadeEjb.getIndexPage</code>: an improvement is achieved by replacing subqueries for phone and email by joins on <code class="notranslate">PersonContactDetail</code> (for <code class="notranslate">PersonFacadeEjb.getIndexList</code> the main query's time was reduced from 4s 195ms to 1s 578ms)</li>
<li>for <code class="notranslate">ImmunizationFacadeEjb.getIndexList</code>: the dataset used for analysis has 2,600,890 entries for immunizations. These are propagated over several joins without reducing the result that take around 1s 30ms each. A solution is not obvious here, since the result set is only reduced after sorting with limit, for which attributes from the joined tables may be necessary. The poor performance seems also to be connected to the use of subselects in the classes <code class="notranslate">FirstVaccinationDate</code>, <code class="notranslate">LastVaccineType</code> and <code class="notranslate">LastVaccinationDate</code> which are attributes of <code class="notranslate">DirectoryImmunization</code></li>
<li>in several places postgres uses a Sequence Scan where an index scan might perform better, e.g., when joining <code class="notranslate">events</code> and <code class="notranslate">location</code> for sample counts (see files <code class="notranslate">explain_samples_count*</code>) or <code class="notranslate">eventparticipant</code> and <code class="notranslate">person</code> for he samples index list (see <code class="notranslate">explain_samples_count.*</code>). Indices on foreign keys are present, the reason for the use of Sequence Scans in these places is subject to further investigation.</li>
</ul></div></div><div role="toolbar" aria-label="Reactions" class="d-flex gap-1 flex-wrap"></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></li><li data-wrapper-timeline-id="IC_kwDOA4AoSc5NfK-3"><div <li>He found that fetching for phone number and email address is causing delays and can probably be improved. But this was not in scope of this ticket.</li>
<li>It was not in scope of this ticket to touch other CoreAdo queries, only work on Person as proof of concept.</li>
<li>The intention of the ticket was to avoid the costly <code class="notranslate">DISTINCT</code> on all selected attributes. We discussed a possible approach with the following two step select.</li>

SELECT DISTINCT * FROM ...(complex generated query) ORDER BY changeDate LIMIT 100 OFFSET 1000;

-- NEW
-- 1. Find person ids of the persons in the page to show (adhere the sorting).
SELECT DISTINCT person.id FROM (SELECT * FROM ...(complex generated query) ORDER BY changeDate) AS sub LIMIT 100 OFFSET 1000;

-- 2. Select attributes into the DTOs, keep sorting

<p dir="auto">-- 1. Find person ids of the persons in the page to show (adhere the sorting).<br>
SELECT DISTINCT person.id FROM (SELECT * FROM ...(complex generated query) ORDER BY changeDate) AS sub LIMIT 100 OFFSET 1000;</p>
<p dir="auto">-- 2. Select attributes into the DTOs, keep sorting<br>
SELECT * FROM ...(complex generated query) WHERE person.id IN (idList); --> (mimic BaseAdoService.getByIds for DTOs, but keep the sorting given by the idList).</p>
</blockquote>
<p dir="auto">There is no easy solution for the first query. Problems:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>the Criteria API does not support multiselect for subqueries</li>
<li>this could be tackled by either handling duplicate Ids Java side, which however interferes with offset an limit. Possible shifts in offset and limit are hard to track and error prone.</li>
<li>alternatively, the Criteria API can be skipped altogether and a raw SQL query can be used. This is somewhat clumsy, however</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto"><a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="1441940323" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/SORMAS-Foundation/SORMAS-Project/issues/10875" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/SORMAS-Foundation/SORMAS-Project/pull/10875/hovercard" href="https://github.com/SORMAS-Foundation/SORMAS-Project/pull/10875">#10875</a> implements an alternative, where Ids of index list persons are read in a first query, omitting all columns but those needed for sorting and thus to handle 'distinct'. So the query to fetch Ids reduces columns to 'id' plus - by default - 'changedate' or - if sort properties era passed - the columns of these sort properties.</p>
<p dir="auto">Testing on the dataset used so far, the query to read Ids of persons associated with cases takes ~230ms, fetching the actual data takes ~20ms (execution time before the refactoring: ~1sec 600ms).</p>
<p dir="auto">Queries and exemplary analysis using <code class="notranslate">explain</code> are provided here:<br>
<a href="https://github.com/hzi-braunschweig/SORMAS-Project/files/9970862/explainSqlPrefetchIds.zip">explainSqlPrefetchIds.zip</a></p></div></div><div role="toolbar" aria-label="Reactions"
